Subject: Scale-Smart observability tier proposal & demo credit ask

Hi Sam —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation the team at AsterHealth needs an observability add-on that: can handle spiky trace ingest during nightly job windows, gives predictable retained traces for HIPAA-adjacent audits, and includes a small set of advanced dashboards for ops teams.

We put together a lightweight proposal I wanted to send over: a new "Scale-Smart" add-on SKU that blends a committed slab (retention + dashboards) with a metered overage stripe for burst tracing. The key points:

- Starter slab: 10 TB of trace storage retained for 30 days + up to 12 dashboard seats.
- Burst credit pool: monthly pool of 1M trace events that auto-consume for spikes; overage billed per 100k events.
- Soft-SLA for trace query latency within slab; fallback to cached results if burst threshold exceeded.
- Intro demo credit: we can provide $10k in observability credits to cover a pilot month of burst traffic and dashboard configuration.

Attached: Scale-Smart-pricing-v1.pdf with rate tables, and an MAP worksheet I filled in for AsterHealth. Also included a short sample SOW outline so procurement has a starting doc.

Would you be comfortable sharing this with procurement? If so, I can also open a quick 30-min call Friday to walk the team through the proposal and answer any redlines.

Best,
Ben

Ben —

Appreciate the proposal and the quick turnaround. A few clarifying questions from our side before I loop procurement:

1) For the burst credit pool — how fast do we consume credits for typical beacon traffic vs. a batch job spike? Any example math would help (events -> credits -> $).
2) The 30-day retention is fine, but for audit purposes we need an archival path (up to 1 year) with cold retrieval. Is that included as an optional add-on or a separate line item?
3) For the dashboard seats — will those be shared seats tied to the Redwoods console or per-user profile? We need role-based access controls mapped to our SSO.

Procurement will ask about termination and data export as well; I can forward the MAP worksheet but they usually want cost buckets broken out by slab vs metered.

If the demo credit is approved we can run a pilot on the upcoming ETL window (12/12) — that'll surface whether bursting is from beacon vs batch.

Thanks,
Sam

Sam —

Thanks for the great questions. Short answers up front, then details below.

1) Burst credit math (example):
- Typical beacon traffic: ~5k events/min -> ~150k events over a 30-minute spike. That would consume ~1.5x of the 100k event billing bucket.
- Batch job (ETL) example: 1.2M events during nightly run -> consume full monthly pool (1M) + 200k overage -> overage = 2 * 100k buckets billed at $0.75 per 100k = $1.50 for the overage period.

2) Archival: Cold archival is an optional add-on. Pricing in the attachment shows $0.01/GB-month for cold retention up to 12 months with on-demand restore (restore latency measured in hours).

3) Dashboard seats: seats are RBAC-enabled and integrate with your SSO (SAML). The Starter slab includes 12 named seats; we can convert to shared seats for cross-team dashboards at no additional charge for the pilot.

Notes on terms & export: data export is supported via encrypted S3 transfer; termination requires a 30-day window for export (we recommend planning the export at least 14 days before contract end). I'll mark those lines in the SOW draft.

Attached again: Scale-Smart-pricing-v1.pdf (rows with the slab vs metered breakout), and the MAP worksheet with the bucket-level costs for procurement.

Next steps I propose:
- I can open a 30-min call with procurement and engineering on Thursday (12/9) or Friday (12/10).
- If you want, we can convert the demo credit to a scoped pilot SOW so procurement has a billable line that can be credited upon completion. That usually smooths legal review.

Would you prefer procurement-friendly SOW + credit, or a straightforward pilot credit?

Best,
Ben

Subject: Fwd: Scale-Smart observability tier proposal & demo credit ask

Kim / Jordan / Laura —

Looping you in for quick alignment. AsterHealth likes the hybrid slab+metered approach but procurement will press on discounting and SOW structure. They asked for: archival pricing detail, burst math (provided), and pilot credit packaged as an SOW line.

Points for commercial:
- They are an SMB to mid-market healthcare customer with HIPAA-adjacent needs; this is a strategic small logo in our healthcare push.
- Requested demo credit $10k — my ask is to cover as a marketing pilot credit; if legal needs it on SOW we should structure it as a refundable credit upon completion.
- Discount request: they asked if we can commit to a 10% on the starter slab if they move to an annual commit within 60 days. My counter: 7% standard, escalate to 10% if they agree to a 12-month reserved capacity add-on.

Questions:
1) Is 7% the max we can offer from seat/retention list price for this segment (LA team target)?
2) If we structure the demo credit as a billable line in the SOW, do we need special wording for refund if pilot does not validate?
3) Any redlines on the archival cold retrieval SLA? Legal typically flags cross-region custody language for healthcare customers.

Tagged you for quick answers since I want to get procurement a clean SOW draft by EOD tomorrow.

—Ben

(Onwarded: earlier email chain attached)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Ben / team —

Quick replies:
1) Commercial: 7% is the standard max for self-serve / SMB bracket; for strategic healthcare mid-market we can authorize 10% one-time for a 12-month commit. Need revenue manager sign-off but I support the ask given renewal/expansion motion.
2) Legal/SOW: we can put the demo credit as a billable line called "Pilot Implementation Credit ($10,000)" refundable against first invoice upon successful pilot acceptance criteria (define acceptance in SOW — I recommend uptake and a short QA checklist). That removes the "marketing credit" ambiguity.
3) Archival SLA: legal will request custody language — propose we offer region-bound cold retention with encrypted export and a 72-hour restore SLA. Flag any cross-region export; recommend we keep export within their chosen cloud region for HIPAA comfort.

I'll loop Legal for the SOW clause; Jordan can you draft the refundable-credit language and include acceptance criteria? Kim, please confirm SSO/RBAC integration notes for the SOW.

Laura
